DI60 is a medical diagnosis code representing subarachnoid hemorrhage (*subaraknoidal blødning*) [^src1]. In the context of the Danish healthcare system's clinical quality databases, specifically the Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), DI60 plays a critical role in monitoring patient safety [^src1]. It is primarily used to track the incidence of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] and severe bleeding complications among patients being treated for [[atrieflimren]] [^src1].

Because patients with atrial fibrillation are often prescribed anticoagulant medications to prevent strokes, they carry an elevated risk of severe bleeding events [^src3]. To measure the safety of these treatments, RKKP utilizes specific ICD-10-DK diagnosis codes, as detailed in their annual methodology and indicator reports [^src2]. DI60 is grouped alongside other intracranial bleeding codes, including [[di61|DI61]], [[di62|DI62]], [[ds064|DS064]], [[ds065|DS065]], and [[ds066|DS066]], to calculate the incidence of intracranial hemorrhage [^src1]. 

Furthermore, DI60 is part of a broader composite indicator used to measure the overall incidence of severe bleeding [^src1]. This comprehensive metric captures a wide spectrum of critical bleeding events, combining the intracranial codes (DI60–DS066) with codes for gastrointestinal bleeding (such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] through [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]) and urinary/respiratory tract bleeding (including [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. By tracking DI60 and its related codes, Danish health authorities can systematically evaluate the risks associated with anticoagulation therapy across different patient demographics and clinical risk profiles [^src3].
